item: The volume job, the single-file restore's log line and the import queue write what they catch with the passphrase taken out, through one set of helpers that take every secret, and the passphrase guard holds seven modules and its own table of them
key_paths: src/monitoring/secret_scrub.py; src/backup/volume_job.py; src/backup/import_queue.py; src/api/backup_v2.py; tests/test_p0_validation.py; tests/test_secret_scrub.py; tests/test_volume_job_scrubs_passphrase.py; tests/test_restore_paths_scrub_passphrase.py; tests/test_repo_invariants.py; docs/CHANGES.md; docs/ledger/LESSONS.md; docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md; docs/ledger/SHIPPED_LOG.md
summary: The coordinator's check of #1318 (B1) named the volume job's own error handlers as the family of the engine's failure line, and its relay asked for the route layer's log lines too. VolumeBackupManager's runners caught Exception with the passphrase (and a restore's corpus passphrase) in scope and wrote the exception's words to the job's error (served by GET /api/backup/v2/volumes/status), the log and the run journal; restore_legacy_path logged its failure with _LOG.exception; and the import queue, which keeps the route's own response text in an item's error (served by the status route, persisted in import_queue.json), stored and logged what its handlers caught. Every such text is now scrubbed where it is made, through one set of helpers in src/monitoring/secret_scrub.py (scrubbed, traceback_text, log_failure) that take every secret the function holds, skip an empty one and withhold a text a later secret's marker would rebuild an earlier one in; the journal's cuts (2000, 8000, 500) come after the scrub; a log line leads with the exception's own line (the error journal cuts a record at 500 characters) and carries the scrubbed traceback as text and no exc_info. The route's responses are left as they are on the condition that no recorder keeps a response's text, which was read: errorlog.note_http_error keeps the status, the method and the path (a test pins that no caller passes a detail), the frontend reporter keeps uncaught UI errors only, and the queue scrubs where it records. The static walk (tests/test_p0_validation.py) holds seven modules, reads corpus_passphrase and the queue's self._passphrase as secrets, accepts status and partial only on a _PhaseError handler (the check's D3), and a coverage test holds its table to every module under src/ that holds the passphrase and writes what it catches, five left out each with its reason. D1 (the crash read's field count in OPEN_QUEUE) and D2 (which argument position a guard reads) of the check are fixed. Tests: 18 for the job, 8 for the route and the queue, the helpers' own and the walk's cases; 32 mutations of the helpers, the route, the queue, the request middleware and the guard and 21 of the job's own scrub sites are each caught. What stays outside is in OPEN_QUEUE.md: the responses and the global handler, runlog.run's journal, a path that is the passphrase, a form that is not the passphrase as typed, what a syntax walk cannot follow, and the columnar store's three records, which ride with the key-derivation change.
